stable_fifo_policy: Latest frame replaces one pending preview but preserves that queue slot's job.created_at. A claimed slot ends; next pending slot starts with a new queue age. Capture timestamp, TTL, production admission, committed priority and in-flight fences unchanged.
limitations: Synthetic observations and delays; no Roboflow latency, quality, upload or rendering measured.
Actual Repository transactions/snapshot reads; no HTTP API or inference-runtime cache/dispatch.
100 ms observer is a benchmark client, not the UI's 1.5 second idle polling interval.
Two cases use the UI's 1.5s poll cadence, without HTTP/upload/browser rendering.
Short trials: descriptive timings, not significance, production capacity or an SLO.
Visible latency conditions on results seen; no-feedback time/AoI expose missing updates.
Offer rates stress the scheduler; they do not match the UI's 0.5 Hz preview cadence.
No failures injected here; worker-death recovery has a separate product fault probe.
Jain counts describe work parity, not demand-normalized fairness; inspect offer counts too.
Stable FIFO adds one indexed pending lookup and one timestamp UPDATE per replacement.
250ms follow-up is the active-preview polling condition, not the full adaptive browser policy.
Browser idle is 1500 ms after feedback/4s timeout; saved pending captures use 650 ms.
No HTTP/upload/rendering measured; browser tests cover wake and idle behavior.
Original FIFO resets queue position; the stable control retains it across replacements.
